target_customer: Software teams that want to embed comments, presence, recording and approvals in their products (later: AI-native apps needing agent and human review)
problem: Building collaboration features such as comments, notifications and multiplayer editing in house takes months.
business_model: Usage and seat-based developer SDK subscriptions

founders.name: Rakesh Goyal
founders.background_notes: YC page: Product Manager at Google for 9 years, launched AR in Google Maps and Search; grew up in India.

investors: Angels from Google, Stripe and SAP

competitors.name: Liveblocks
competitors.what: API for real-time collaboration in products; named on Velt's own site as a rival
competitors.funding_then: 1.4M pre-seed in September 2021; 5M seed in March 2022

competitors.name: Cord
competitors.what: Single API for Slack-like collaboration features in any app; named on Velt's site
competitors.funding_then: 17.5M led by Index Ventures in October 2021

technical_complexity.rationale: A drop-in SDK for comments and presence needs solid front-end and real-time infrastructure; CRDT multiplayer editing added later raises the difficulty.

defensibility.rationale: Once integrated, data and UI lock customers in, but Liveblocks and Cord offered similar SDKs and customers can build in house.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found; rivals kept funding themselves and Velt later repositioned around AI agent review.

market_need_then: Figma and Google Docs raised user expectations for collaboration, and two funded rivals had launched around 2021, which implies demand for embeddable collaboration infrastructure.

rebrands.why: Not stated in opened sources; YC lists the older slug snippyly

branding.community_and_virality: Frequent Product Hunt launches and npm SDK; no merch or fan content found.

brand_strength.rationale: Repeated Product Hunt and YC launches and a TechCrunch article, but a modest developer brand.

pivots.from: Commenting and collaboration SDK (earlier names Snippyly and Superflow)
pivots.to: Agent and human review and governance layer for AI-native apps
pivots.why: Company repositioned toward AI agent approval flows; date not given.

outcome_analysis: Velt sells an SDK for embedding collaboration and now AI review flows, and lists customers such as Google, Pendo and HeyGen on its site. It disclosed only a 2.77M seed, and funding since is unknown. Funded rivals Liveblocks and Cord make defensibility modest, but the company is Active with 15 staff and repeated launches.
notes: TechCrunch dated 2023-12-04 says the seed closed last March (so 2023-03); other aggregators date it 2022-03. Seedtable lists 2023-03. Competitor funding sources come from search results (Finsmes and Tech.eu were not opened). Co-founder Solene Oudet appears only in an aggregator (yespress) and is not listed. Founding year: YC says 2020. The relationship between Superflow and Velt is unclear in the YC page. No acquisition, layoff or shutdown news found.
